translations.text: In the desert, in my father's house, to repent of my many faults.
And this is what is in my heart: even if I will not be worthy to see the Lord face to face, openly, in the place where I am going, because I am a sinful person,

nevertheless, I will strive to please him secretly on earth, since he does not prevent anyone—neither me nor anyone else—from repenting or intending to repent. And if I go to him, he rejoices in his compassion to have mercy on me in my poverty.
Only, this is how I pray in my house, confessing my sins before the Lord. I say, weeping, “Let me be worthy to see him in the place where I am going, and let him punish me with fire.”
But I believe that he will have mercy on me through your prayers, brothers.

And I think that those who strive to please him on earth through prayers, fasts, nights of watching, praises, much meditation, and willingness to learn, with complete submission and humility, with complete obedience and wisdom, and with all the other deeds,
they are also the ones who will please him in the place where they are going, and they are the ones who will see him face to face in that place.
But those who are always disobedient, who hate God, who are arrogant, boastful, unteachable, hard-hearted, slow to understand, insolent, ungrateful, and defiled,

and whose consciences are polluted and burn against them with strife, hatred, and hostility, with scoffing and rejection of the word of God, with grumbling, faultfinding, boasting, sexual immorality, all the many other things, and every evil deed—
those who do these things and these other things will never be worthy to please the Lord Jesus on earth through faith,
much less to see him face to face in heaven, in the place where they are going. Indeed, it is people of this kind whom he will burn in a fire that never goes out.
I said these things to you to tell you that my wish is to remain in my house, repenting all the days of my life.

But now, in turn, I tell you that I wish to remain among my brothers, the children of God and the children of my fathers, so that we may benefit one another. For this is God's will, and this is the will of my fathers, while I have been in the desert for more than a hundred years.
And this is how I wish to bear everything that comes upon me, as though I were doing nothing.

The elder and all the elders are the ones who labor in everything. And we are grateful to the brothers who share our labor, who obey our word in everything they are able to do, and who give us peace of mind through complete submission, working for their salvation with fear and trembling.
We know who they all are, from the least of them to the greatest.
Therefore, may God bless them.
And may he protect them from every evil deed and give them rest in every way in heaven, in the place where they are going.
But those who are disobedient in everything, who reject the word of the Lord through their disobedience and their reliance on themselves alone—we know who they are.

For this reason, may the Lord forgive them, because they are our brothers and our fellow members, and because they too are weary in their ignorance, and because we too are distressed about them, because they have not served us for our bodily comfort.
We are grateful to those who offer us their handful in the evening, or indeed any of their possessions, in their love.
And it is the Lord who will repay them according to their good deeds.
Nor are we grieved because those people have spoken a word against us, for we deserve it.
Therefore, being as they are, they do not prevail against us by speaking words against us, or privately among themselves, grumbling or finding fault without cause.

If only the Lord would also grant us to turn our cheek to the one who strikes us on it! And if it should happen that we too are killed for the name of our God, may we willingly say, “Lord, do not charge them with this sin.”

But we are troubled and grieve day and night over those who disobey the gospel of our Lord Jesus, who says, “Unless you turn and become like these little children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.”
See now how clearly the ignorance of those among us who consider themselves wise has been revealed, whether male or female, great or small.
Brothers and sisters, I say these things so that no one among us here, or among you yourselves, will lose heart while bearing with those beside them.
For the Lord is the one who will give you your reward. Therefore, do not be distressed if they mock you or torment you and say evil things against you.

It is no wonder if those people insult you, spit in your face, or strike you on the head, like the messenger of Satan, as it is written: “We are hungry, we are thirsty, we are naked, we are struck, we are unsettled, and we toil. When they persecute us, we endure them. When they slander us, we appeal to them.”
Rather, the remarkable thing is not to let them stumble because of you through any evil deed, as it is written.
We are not saying these things to you to shame you.

Rather, we are instructing you as a beloved brother, so that we may not be condemned with the world, and so that we may escape the pronouncement of our prophet: “Look, I will bring disasters upon this people and upon the fruit of their disobedience, because they did not pay attention to my word and abandoned my law.”

Therefore, I beg you, brothers and sisters, to keep yourselves away from every fight and every quarrel, every evil deed, and every bodily desire that wars against your souls, so that we may circumcise the uncircumcision of our hard heart, and so that the Lord may make you grow in every good deed to do his will for him, as he works in us what is pleasing in his sight.
For this is God's will: your purification, so that we may be holy for him and love one another as he commanded us according to the Scriptures.
What is circumcision of the heart, or what is uncircumcision?

Those who continually live in hardness of heart, stiff-neckedness, dullness of understanding, ignorance, disobedience, obstinacy, fighting, quarreling, envy, hatred, defilement, and every evil deed are the ones who are uncircumcised in their hearts and also in their ears, according to the Scriptures.
But those who live at all times in humility, joyfulness, patience, love, and willingness to learn, with complete submission, complete obedience, and every kind of usefulness,
[?] or a woman among us who pours water over their head to wash their face, out of a desire to preserve for themselves the memory of the hair on their head, in vanity and a passion for pleasure.

Cursed is any man or woman among us who wickedly washes their feet out of desire, secretly dips them in water, or secretly anoints them with oil, without first consulting the elder here among us, or without the woman elder among you.

Cursed is any man or woman among us who sets their heart on a garment, a cloak, bedding, a hood, or sandals, wanting them to be well made for them and saying, “They are ours,” when they have not all received an equal share together, from the greatest to the least.
Cursed is any man or woman among us who favors their own blood relatives over strangers and orphans among us, whether in food, clothing, any other possessions, or any other matter.

Cursed is any man or woman among us who eats any stolen food outside the rule laid down for us, whether [?] of fish, cooked fish, salted fish, an egg, cheese, [?], milk, or any other food outside the rule.
Therefore, do not let anyone deceive us, either here with us or there with you, into touching or tasting any of these things at all.
Do not even let us think about them at all.
Nor let us desire them so as to keep them for ourselves, just as our fathers observed these things.
They too suffered illness and endured very great hardships, but it was for our sake, so that we would not die.
They did not touch them, nor did they taste any of them,
thereby defiling themselves in any way, whether they were away from home or in the congregation.

And anyone among us who sins or will sin secretly, either here with us or there with you, and does not confess the sin they have committed—all these curses will come upon them. And also those who defiantly offer the Eucharistic offering anywhere in our vicinity, whether they are in communion with us or live near us without being in communion with us,

and anyone who defiantly offers the Eucharistic offering anywhere in our vicinity, except within our congregations, where all the brothers assemble, and at our father's monastery, where the church is in the desert, will be cursed.
Our vicinity extends from the canal north of the village of Atripe southward to the canal south of the house of our elderly father Apa Bishoy, the place where he first lived in the desert.
Everyone who settles near us will be bound by the rules laid down for all the brothers who assemble together.
Four Saturdays each year: these are what our father established for us.
Everyone living in the desert in our vicinity must also assemble with the brothers, so that they come together, unless prevented by illness.
But anyone living in the desert who is unwilling to live according to the ordinances our fathers laid down for us—
if they are in our congregations, we will expel them from them, whether they are a man or a woman.
And if they are in the desert in our vicinity, we will assemble, go to the place where they are, and drive them away from our neighborhood.
But if they defiantly resist us, we will descend upon the place where they live and forcibly drive them out of it.
But we will take care not to strike them, because that could cause a death.
And we will descend upon the place where they lived and demolish it down to its foundations, so that no one will ever live in it and cause offense to their neighbor.

Furthermore, those among us who at any time flee from the elder and go to bishops without permission, to have hands laid on them in defiance, will be cursed. For obedience is better than their presenting Eucharistic offerings in disobedience and lack of discipline.

But no one may act out of envy toward anyone who lives according to the rules laid down for us and expel them, whether they are in the desert in our vicinity or in the congregation with us, either here with us or there with you.

But if a time comes when sin gains power over those living in this place, at that time, because of the blindness of heart that will come upon everyone who transgresses the commandments laid down for them here in this desert where we now are,
then at that time anyone who wishes to flee to the desert, anywhere, to save themselves is free from all these curses.

so that he may settle on this mountain, and also offer an offering in the place he wishes, in the fear of God, taking care not to offer a sacrifice in any other place except the place that the Lord God has chosen for himself, according to the Scriptures.
And those who turn toward us to live with us, whether men or women, or those in the desert around us—everyone who shares in our fellowship, among us, here with us or there with you—
and do not renounce everything they possess, whether gold, silver, copper, clothing, or any other possessions, will be cursed, because they have not taken up their cross to follow the Lord.
And whoever sets his heart on any of the things they renounced so that they might come under the bond of God's fellowship and service to the poor,
so that he turns back, denies his commitment, and seeks a way to take them again, will be cursed, having become like Ananias and his wife Sapphira,
and like Cain and the others with whom the Lord has not been pleased, from the beginning until now.
And whoever gives things away secretly to the elder and the brothers will be cursed before God.
And whoever secretly takes oil, copper, clothing, or anything else and gives it to his relatives outside, or to any other person outside, will be cursed before the Lord.
And whoever secretly and deceitfully gives things to his neighbor among us, here with us or there with you, whether food, clothing, shoes, a belt, or absolutely any other things, in secret,

without first informing the elder here with us, or without first informing the female elder there with you, will be cursed, because they have violated the commandments that our fathers entrusted to us:

that no one, whether man or woman, should secretly and deceitfully give anything to their neighbor without its being authorized by the elder here with us, or by the female elder appointed for you there among you.

And whoever shaves himself, or those who shave another person among us, whether man or woman, without authorization, will be cursed, because they have violated the commandments that our fathers entrusted to us.

And whoever removes a thorn from the foot of someone among us, whether man or woman, without necessity and without authorization, will be cursed, because they have dishonored the commandments that our fathers entrusted to us.
The necessity is this: if we are away from home or traveling along a road, far from the assembly, or alternatively,
if we are in the assembly and a thorn is troubling someone's foot or hand, then, because of the urgency of the pain, the person near him shall remove it for him in the fear of God.

And this is how it shall be for someone away from home, someone traveling along the road, and his neighbor, or any other brother: the person near him shall remove it for him with fear and great trembling.

Whoever keeps defiled thoughts in his heart, or harbors an impure desire in his spirit while being shaved, or while he himself shaves his neighbor, or while a thorn is being removed from his foot, or while he himself removes a thorn from his neighbor's feet, will be cursed, whether a man or a woman.
And those who sleep two together on one mat, or those who sleep close enough to touch or cling to one another at all with lustful passion, will be cursed, whether men or women.
And those who allow themselves to sit close to their neighbor while there is an impure desire in their heart will be cursed, whether men or women.

And those who get up again from their sleeping places and approach the sleeping places of those beside them, to touch those beside them with passionate desire while they are sleeping and do not know—or, instead, while they know and put up with one another, talking [?] while

urinating into a flask or a pot, or into any other similar vessel, without having been instructed to do so by the elder, except only in the quarters of the sick and the elderly who are advanced in years—and these others must ask the elder.

And if a need arises for some among us to do something like this, to urinate into any vessel of this kind because of an injury or a sore that has developed on someone’s feet, so that he cannot walk outside, they must consult the elder.
And apart from these cases, if small children or any other people urinate into any vessel of this kind, they will be cursed.
Cursed is anyone who attributes a sinful deed to his neighbor through slander,
without knowing how to distinguish the truth, but out of hatred saying what is not so, whether it is a man or a woman.
Cursed is anyone who says deceitfully, “I saw a dream in which so-and-so and so-and-so were defiling themselves with every kind of evil deed,” whether it is a man or a woman.

Cursed are all who practice deceit in any of the Lord’s congregations, causing God to become angry with a great multitude and turn his face away from them in wrath because of the wickedness of those who practice lawlessness among us, secretly or openly.

And woe to those because of whom God will become disgusted and seek a way to leave their midst, like a righteous person who has sought a way to leave a people behind because of their evil deeds, according to the prophet’s saying: “Who will give me a remote dwelling place in the wilderness, so that I may leave this people behind and go far away from them?”

But blessed are all those through whom God will be comforted, so that he is willing to remain among them, like a righteous person who has been comforted by faithful people and has been willing to remain among them at all times, because the Lord himself is also among them at all times because of their true and righteous deeds.

And anyone among us who sees a deceitful deed involving impurity, theft, or any other sin that leads to death, but does not tell me who it is or what those evil deeds are—all these curses will come upon them from God, whether it is a man or a woman.
And all the others who ought to be cursed in this letter but whom we have not cursed—look, they are all recorded in the documents written earlier.
And I will tell you what the holy words of our Lord Jesus, written in the Scriptures and in this letter, are like.
They are like lamps that have been lit in dark places.
And they are like daylight.
And the senseless, who go to great extremes in foolishness, are like bats.
And just as bats—that is, flying mice—fall down or flee into the darkness or into hollow places whenever they see the light of the flame of lamps and the light of day.

This, again, is how the senseless and those who go to great extremes in foolishness will fall downward, or into their passions and desires and the darkness of their false knowledge, in the face of all the words of our Lord—whether those in the Scriptures or those in this letter, and not these alone, but also all the others written on these sheets that have been written from the beginning.
Again, the holy words of our Lord Jesus are like the light of lamps in the hands of a wise person,
giving him light in dark places as he does his work.
As it is written, “Your word is a lamp for my feet.”
And they are like daylight.
Whoever pays attention to them will not stumble, according to the Scriptures: “Whoever walks in the daytime does not stumble.”
Therefore, blessed are the children of light, who walk confidently in complete submission, complete obedience, and every good deed.
But woe to the children of darkness, who walk in every kind of disobedience and every kind of ignorance,
running into, or down into, the darkness of every evil deed, like bats that fly into, or down into, places of very deep darkness.
Why did the Lord God say through his saints, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him, and if he is thirsty, give him something to drink”?
And why, in turn, did he say, “If your brother does not listen to you, let him be to you like a Gentile and a tax collector”?

When he says, “Do every good thing for your enemies,” according to the commandment, he wants the good person who belongs to God to perfect his goodness through the wickedness of the evil person who belongs to the sinner Satan.
For, in place of the evil person's wickedness, the good person's goodness removes the hostile person's wickedness.
When a person repays evil with good, he fully expresses God's divinity.
But when a person repays good with evil, he fully expresses the godlessness of the godless devil.

When he says, “If your brother does not listen to you, let him become an enemy to you, like someone you have never seen,” the Lord first wants us to cut him off from ourselves after we have rebuked him, so that perhaps he may come to his senses after becoming like a stranger for God's sake, although he is our brother, and turn back and repent. Then we are to forgive him up to seven times seventy times, provided he does not repeat the sin for which we intended to cut him off from ourselves.
But if he is unwilling to turn away from the sin for which we intended to cut him off from ourselves, we will cut him off from ourselves. He must not return to us, and we must not love him.
Instead, he will be an enemy to us for God's sake, although he is our brother.
In this way, the person who loves God reveals his wholehearted devotion to the Lord: he has loved him more than his brother, and more than his father and mother.

For it is a great sign of perfection for a person to cut off his brother, his son, his daughter, his father, his mother, or anyone else belonging to him, for God's sake, whenever they sin against the one who created them, who is God.

And it is a great sign of strength for a person to love his enemies for God's sake, and to pray for those who pursue him to harm him, and, for God's sake, to bless those who curse him and sin against him.
And this is how he said it: “Let your brother be to you like a Gentile and a tax collector,” for God's sake, whenever he sins before the Lord.
But your enemy who sins against you—you are to love him and bless him for God's sake.
But we too, brothers, insofar as we share fellowship with one another, are children of one person, who is God.
And we are children of one mother, who is the heavenly Jerusalem, according to the Scriptures.
Are our father and mother, who brought us into the world and raised us physically, then better than our Lord Jesus, our father, and our true mother?
He is the one who brought us to birth through his holy blood.
[?] suffering [?] greatly [?]
with every suffering upon me.
But concerning the young girls about whom we have heard:
that they will rush toward one another with fleshly desire.
Tell me about them accurately, so that I may understand,
and I will tell you what you should do to them.
But again, regarding this woman whom you mentioned,
that she should go to the place you assigned to her
to do her work there, when she said to you,
“If you take me from this place to that one,
I will not do the work I am doing.”
And if she really refuses,
then tell me again, and I will instruct you about what you should do to her.
But all of you, if you conceal from us any deceitful act among you and do not tell us about it,
you are stirring up Satan against yourselves,
and you yourselves are turning God's help away from you.
Look, I have sent the elder to you again this time, as long as we are alive.
As they are, like senseless animals.
But the Lord is compassionate and merciful; he will show mercy
to everyone who has gone to him and believes in him, because they have spoken his name at some time
and have done something good for his name in his presence for a day.
And yet they are ignorant;
they have not understood the Lord's will.
Therefore, perhaps the written words will be fulfilled concerning them,
so that they receive a little punishment from the Lord as ignorant servants, and the deaf man will see that they are blind.
But you who sin, or who will soon sin among us—the Lord curses you, because if you were blind, you would have no sin.
But now you say, “We see that your sin has risen against you.”
Therefore [?] leave you like a [?] land with no water in it,
and like a garden and a vineyard that their owners have abandoned, no longer taking any care of them at all.
For there is no fruit on their trees, nor are there grapes on their vines, nor figs on their fig trees.
Instead, they were also withering, having dried up, as the Scriptures say.
And in this way they became prey, for strangers to seize them [?].
This is also your situation: God's angels will abandon you and will not watch over you at all,
because there is no understanding, no fear of God, and no truth within you.
Otherwise you would never have sinned against a commandment.
But because the fear of the Lord is not before your eyes, you yourselves take part in the fruitless works of darkness.
And in this way you have become prey.
into his presence, into his holy assemblies,
so that you may live the life of the angels
and bear abundant fruit, as it is written,
so that the Lord God may bless you, because you yourselves have blessed him without deceit, just as the holy angels bless him.
And he himself, in turn, will pour all his blessings down upon them with power.
The Lord blesses you so that you may be holy and be delivered from every evil deed.

And he will give you glory through himself, just as he gave glory to his angels, because you yourselves have glorified him through your good deeds in the purity of your body, just as all his angels also glorified him.
May the Lord bless you and honor you through himself, through all his angels, through all the holy guests, and through everyone who comes to you.
Just as you are called angels, although you are human beings,
yet you live the life of God's angels and make yourselves like the prophets, the apostles, and all the saints—not merely through your outward appearance and an empty name,
like the many who adopt the appearance of devotion to God
but deny its power, but through all the sufferings you endure for the name of the Lord Christ Jesus.
And so that you may be worthy of the promises he made to his prophets, his apostles, and all his saints.
Therefore the Lord will bless [?]
Therefore no property will remain because of his sins, since he will not repent.
What is repentance except for us to turn away from every deceit and every disobedience, the root of every evil deed?
These things and all things like them—those who read them and those who hear them, or those who teach others from them,
while they themselves transgress all of them—these
of this sort, whether they are men,
or whether it is a woman, strip themselves naked
and curse their own souls,
Therefore everyone who reads all the Lord's Scriptures is cursed
while committing sexual immorality, defilement, pollution, theft, lies, and false oaths,
and they do not repent of the impurity and pollution they have committed.
But all the more cursed are all those who reach out their hands toward the holy Gospels of our Lord Jesus
and open them with their hands, which are full of every kind of filth and impurity,
to read them while living in great deceit, jealousy, hatred, hostility toward others, and every kind of especially wicked deed, with many sins
that lead to death, as it is written:
“There is a sin that leads to death.”
And it is not possible to plead with God on behalf of those who commit them, asking him to forgive them,
because it is not one brother, nor two,
who have done what is especially evil in the sight of the Lord.
For this reason I tell you, brothers,
that all those who read the Lord’s books
and meditate on the words of God’s Scriptures
since they do not heal themselves through their own deeds.
are brothers of the one who destroys himself, as it is written:
“By what does a person destroy himself,
except by bringing an abomination into his house,
so that he becomes an abomination in God’s sight, suffering great destruction?”
What is our house, if not our congregation
and we ourselves? What is the abomination that we will bring into our house, if not sexual immorality, filth, theft, falsehood, and every evil deed?
Who is the brother of the one who destroys himself,
if not the one who does these things and many others,
and the one who has established for himself two measures and a dishonest measuring vessel?
Who is the one who destroys himself, if not the evil demon, Satan, the son of destruction,
the enemy of everyone who loves our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God?
I tell you that just as two measures are an abomination to the Lord,
and a dishonest measuring vessel is not good in his sight,
Likewise, the person who is double-minded in his endurance is an abomination to God,
neither is a deceitful person good in God’s sight.
as is the person who curses someone who pleads with God.
while disobeying his law.
Therefore, if they stretch out their hands to him, he will turn his face away from them.
And if they multiply their pleas, he will not listen to them, according to the Scriptures.
But consider: if we were the ones being sinned against,
And again they pray to us as they do to God.
and we were to put up with those who plead with us while throwing dust in our faces,
would we not become very angry?
And how could God not be angry with us when we pray to him,
while also provoking him with all our evil deeds?
But we will say that many of the saints put up with those who insulted them and threw dust in their faces,
and, when many of them were killed, they blessed their killers, crying out to God
not to count against them the sins they had committed against them.
But consider also
how many of them God ordered to be punished,
And how much of the blood of those they killed will come upon them!
just as Solomon the righteous punished that man
who had thrown dust in his father's face.
And just as our Lord Jesus said that all the righteous blood shed on the earth,
from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, should come upon those murderers.
Therefore I tell you that, just as all the saints were patient with those who persecuted them,
putting up with them,
leaving room for wrath on the day of wrath, as it is written,
and just as that man threw dust in the face of our father David,
and David was patient with him
until the day when he handed him over to his son
to punish him with a just judgment because he had not repented,
so too God is patient with those who sin.
Or those who will sin before him until the end of the ages.
And on the day when he will punish us with severe punishments in the blazing fiery furnace through his holy Son Jesus,
to whom his Father gave authority to carry out judgment.
As it is written, “The Father will judge no one.”
But he gave all judgment to the Son.
Do not now, brothers, let our hearts run wild with foolishness, like disobedient little children from whom the rod and instruction are far away, as it is written.
But just as a father disciplines his son with a rod,
wanting to save his soul from death because he loves him very much,
so let us also discipline ourselves through fear of standing before the Lord’s judgment seat.
And let us earnestly instruct ourselves by remembering the punishments,
knowing that we cannot endure the blazing fiery furnace, hunger, thirst, and many other afflictions.
See: everyone who learns a trade,
if they are not disciplined, does not complete their work properly,
whether those working at looms, carpenters, blacksmiths, or those in all the other trades.
For this reason, first of all, blessed is the Lord, because he teaches us through sufferings and scourges, as it is written,
wishing us to know him rightly, as it is written,
For the Lord disciplines the one he loves,
and he whips every son whom he will accept.
And we too should instruct ourselves in the fear of the Lord,
so that we may learn to love one another
and walk in peace with a brother.
After this, let us discipline the little boys and little girls among us with a rod,
so that they may learn to fear God
and keep his commandments, so that they may receive abundant blessing as wise people, according to the Scriptures.
For in congregations that leave little children alone while they [?] within them, wrath and anger from God are being prepared
by those to whom they have been entrusted, for themselves, because they did not teach them to guard themselves against every impurity and every evil deed.
Therefore, instruct the little girls among you
to guard their bodies against every defilement.
And to make them control their tongues, so that they do not engage in joking, laughter, loose behavior, or excessive idle talk.
Older women among you, or young girls who have grown up,
who disobey those who instruct them according to the commandment,
and answer back to their parents among you—send word to us about them.
And I myself will deal with them, to oppose disobedience and arrogance,
which Satan says within them, as it is written.
For we are ready to punish every act of disobedience.
and every proud thing that rises up against the knowledge of God.
And if you do not send word to us about them,
know that you are sinning against the one who created you.
There is a kind of godliness in people's eyes that is godlessness in God's eyes, namely this:
People who cover up one another’s sins.
when no one instructs any of them,
and none of them rebukes those around him,
So that he, in turn, will not rebuke him, saying, “It is godliness,” although it is godlessness.
because they tolerate the transgressor in all his evil deeds,
because he has humbled himself before them so that they will leave him to the desires of his evil heart,
saying, “God is patient,
and he does not become angry with those who sin.”
They are bringing destruction and ruin upon themselves along with those people, like those upon whom God brought a flood of great waters,
because he was intensely angry with them, in great wrath;
and like all the others whom he has wiped out from his presence, from the beginning until today, because they sinned against him;
and like all those whom he will curse in great anger, sending them down into the fiery furnace that burns at the end of the age,
because they did not keep his commandments.
For God is not unjust when he brings, or will bring, his wrath in anger and a curse upon everyone at any time who sins, or will sin, against him.
May that never be!
Rather, what we receive because of our evil deeds is indeed deserved.
Therefore, according to the Scriptures, anyone who sleeps with any animal is cursed,
or indeed with any living creature at all.
Cursed is anyone who touches the hand of the person beside him
or his foot, or any other part of his body, with lustful passion.
Cursed is anyone who gazes into the face of the person beside him with lust.
Cursed is anyone who stretches himself out on his belly on the ground
to make wicked movements while thoughts of sexual immorality torment him through the pleasure of filthy lust,
Cursed is anyone who runs to his neighbor, among us or among you yourselves, to wink at him.
and who also gives a kiss with lustful passion
and with unrestrained laughter amid idle behavior.
Cursed is anyone who makes merry among little boys in our community.
And cursed is any woman who makes merry among little girls in your community,
because they have despised the word of God, according to [?].
Then Lot [?] our [?] to entrust them to us, while we take pleasure among little boys and among little girls.
Nor, indeed, should any of us, according to the word of the apostles, allow any obscenity, foolish talk, or joking to be found among us—things that are inappropriate.
Cursed is anyone who has filthy lust in his heart
while feeling the body of the person beside him
or anointing him with oil when he is sick.
Cursed is a little boy or a little girl, or an adult man or an adult woman, who has filthy lust in their heart
while the person beside them anoints them [?] bathes them during their illnesses.
Cursed is anyone who anoints the person beside him
or bathes him when he is sick among us, without the elder.
Cursed is any woman who anoints the woman beside her
or bathes her when she is sick among you as well, without the female elder appointed for you.
Cursed is anyone who bathes the person beside him
or anoints him when he is sick among us, in our community or in yours [?]
inside [?], or any of them alone, without another one of them there with them, or two others.
Cursed is anyone who allows a woman to sleep in the doorway
or around the synagogue in our community without the elder, or who allows anyone at all to sleep there.
Cursed is anyone who allows a man to sleep inside the outer door of your congregation among you.
Except for the elders appointed among you [?] elders first among us.
So that he defiles himself while he [?].
Cursed is a [?] within [?] while he [?] and [?] door [?] among [?] so that he [?] and [?] those who [?] perhaps [?] for him.
[?] coming to [?] among [?] your [?] flesh [?] you [?] because of [?].
[?] until [?] which is [?].
For it is our comfort and the place to which we came.
They will become strangers to us, as other brothers, because they sought a way to make their brothers stumble and to cause them offense through their obedience and endurance.
Therefore, if these people and others like them provoke God among us or among you yourselves, let us cut them off from us if they will not repent after we have instructed them with brotherly justice.
Lest God [?] because [?] cover up [?].

And [?] for us to put [?] on them because they are our brothers, or because they are our companions, or because they are our children, so that we do not throw them out of God's house if they sin against him.
Lest the Lord cast us away from himself because we honored them [?], covering up sins, or those who sin, or those who will sin [?] among us or among you yourselves.
Only those who committed sexual immorality and defilement and many acts of deceit within [?] their [?], coming in to us again to settle in the place within the Lord's congregations.
I tell you, brothers, that if I sin before the Lord, it is to your advantage before God
and it is also a good thing for you to cut me off from among you
and throw me out of the Lord's congregations, rather than tolerate me in my sins and my wickedness
and have the Lord become angry with you because of [?] and bring great evils upon you in anger and wrath
and [?] you because of me, because I sinned against him.
Therefore, whether it is I or this person, whether it is a man or a woman, if we sin within the Lord's congregations,
it is to our advantage to be thrown out of the Lord's holy place. Perhaps the Lord will forgive us
and have mercy on us because we received a visitation, chastisement, and disgrace on earth, rather than [?] harm ourselves through our sins
and have the Lord utterly disgrace us with visitation and chastisement forever in the place to which we will go
and pour out his wrath and anger upon us in Hades, in the furnace of blazing fire.
Let none of us now cover up sins and those beside him, when we know about them among us or among you yourselves,
and kill one another because of a fleshly desire that will come to an end.

Indeed, snakes and reptiles, all wild beasts, and animals without understanding love one another, each according to its own kind. But they do not do so because of God, or to escape punishment, or to enter a place of rest.
Therefore, brothers, let us not love one another in word and tongue alone, as those who went out from among us loved us in word and tongue.
But let us love one another in deed and truth, ready to die and to live together, like all those whose words we read—the prophets and all the saints.

Nor should we cover up one another’s sins and make God angry with us, as many congregations covered up one another’s sins and became estranged from God without knowing it, because they did not stop doing harmful deeds.

Indeed, a small group of people who keep the Lord’s commandments is honored before him, like Noah and his household, more than a great multitude that transgresses before the Lord and is despised before him, like all those whom he drowned in the abundant waters of the flood in anger and wrath.
And let us not neglect those who are among us, lest God become angry with us.
Nor should we let ourselves be deceived by what happens to us into unbelief, so that we put our trust in anyone else to be saved through him, except God alone.
Nor should we let ourselves be enslaved by tricks involving different kinds of food, so that we grumble over food for the body.
Nor should we fall into the sickness of demons and lie down in defilement and adultery,
so that God becomes angry with us and hands us over to a perverse mind, filled with every kind of faultfinding, judging rashly because of our insatiability and ingratitude.
Nor should we mock one another by saying, “You are not really in that condition,” lest God become angry with us in our ignorance. For who can understand what is inside a person?
It is the Lord who knows what is hidden.
He is also the one who will judge the person who lives in falsehood and the person who lives in the conditions caused by demons.
And he is the one who will judge everyone who despises those who live among us or among you yourselves.
Do not let these people give anything that we do not need, lest the Lord disgrace us as deceivers,
and we become hateful in his sight.

Nor should we forget what is required of us according to the rules our fathers laid down for us, according to the capacity and strength of our bodies, lest we become people who despise one another before the Lord, and the Lord despise us in his presence and in the presence of his angel.

Nor should we misrepresent ourselves to anyone among us or among you yourselves out of favoritism, whether concerning our illnesses or our states of rest, when that is not our actual condition, lest the Lord deal with us according to what is in our hearts
and disgrace us as people who violate the rights of orphans, widows, and strangers, for there is no favoritism with him.

Therefore, do not let Satan deceive us through enslavement, so that some among us love their sons, their daughters, their brothers, their parents, or any other relatives by birth more than the orphans and strangers who have no one here among us, lest the Lord count us as strangers before him and as enemies in his presence.
For this reason, those who have sons or daughters, brothers or sisters, or parents—whether a father or a mother—or any relatives by birth are greatly disgraced before God.
And they be forgotten—that is, orphans and strangers who have no one here among us.

It is an abomination in a place like this for those who have someone here to discriminate against strangers and orphans in favor of their own relatives by birth, showing favoritism in food, clothing, during their illnesses or when they are not ill, or in any other matter.
Therefore, guard yourselves very carefully against making distinctions between your relatives by birth and strangers and orphans who have no one here among us.
For this is a great abomination before the Lord.
And whoever does these things will be unclean before God, your judge, and before orphans, strangers, and everyone toward whom you show favoritism in any matter, from a garment to a fringe.

Especially in food and clothing, or during their illness—or even when they are not sick. And whoever favors his own blood relatives over them, among us or among you yourselves, in any matter, from a small handful to the smallest, most worthless thing, whether fruit from trees or garden vegetables,

especially oil, wine, or cooked food, and down to a bowl, a mat, a bed, or a lamp during their illness—and whoever favors his own blood relatives over strangers and orphans, showing favoritism in these things we have mentioned and in everything like them, will be cursed before God and people.

Therefore, do not let anyone deceive us in a matter like this, so that we favor our own blood relatives over strangers and orphans in any matter, showing favoritism by caring for them, serving them, or staying with them during their illness without our having been assigned to do so, lest the one who created us become angry with us
and pour his curse down upon us, just as he cursed many peoples because of deeds like these,
among whom each person neglected his neighbor in his illness, his distress, his need, and every other matter.
I say these things so that some among us, whether here with us or there with you yourselves, will not sin before the Lord through these very evil deeds, namely favoritism:
favoring our own blood relatives over strangers and orphans who have no one among us.
Therefore, do not favor one person over another among you in any matter or with any item, lest God become angry with you.
Instead, care for one another with fear and trembling, so that the Lord may bless you and make you grow in every good thing.

What, then, is favoritism? If anyone among us or among you yourselves gives any additional item to anyone among us beyond what has been allotted to them, without first informing me, they are sinning before the Lord.
And this is favoritism.
But if I give something to someone, whether an old man, an older woman, a little boy, or a little girl, whether they are your blood relatives, strangers, or orphans who have no one among us,
and I tell you to give them an additional item, whether a garment, a mat, a sheepskin, something to eat, or indeed any item at all,
and I give them these things with my own hands, or tell the elder to give them these things,
or you yourselves give them these things when we send them to you, no one will find grounds for accusing me.
Nor will there be any cause for stumbling or any sinful deed among us, whether here with us or there with you yourselves.
Therefore, do not do anything beyond what we authorize.
It has not been laid down [?] that you should give any additional item to anyone among you beyond what has been allotted [?], without first informing us.
It is not because you are to submit to us as though the Lord were not [?].

But so that you may be without sin, live without grumbling, misgivings, or any faultfinding, with no one among us here or among you yourselves finding fault, grumbling, or slandering his neighbor because of this worthless practice, namely favoritism.

Therefore, let no one among us, here with us or with you yourselves, show favoritism to anyone in any matter, whether in your dining place or in your place for the sick, lest you become a stumbling block to one another through malicious slander.
Otherwise the written saying will apply to you: “You sat and slandered your brothers and put a stumbling block before your mother's children.” But

if people among us here or among you yourselves take care of their sons, their daughters, their brothers, their parents, or any of their relatives by blood more than the orphans and strangers among us,
then [?] these [?] under [?] [?] will [?] become an abomination before God,
and be accursed before Jesus,
who [?] the stranger, the local resident, and everyone alike.
But if this statement is a lie, and this great abomination does not exist among us here or among you yourselves, with no one among us here or among you yourselves
taking care of their sons, their daughters, their brothers, their sisters, their parents, or any of their relatives by blood more than the orphans and strangers who have no relatives here among us,
then let those who say these things among us or among you yourselves become an abomination before Jesus and be accursed before God,
because they have committed a sin that is doubled against them as a curse and punishment forever,
because they have said what is not true.
Therefore, let us not provoke God's anger against us through actions like these: your favoring your own relatives by blood over those who have no relatives here among us,
or your saying what is not true, lying before God,
[?] [?] [?] secretly against one another,
saying, “The person who has relatives in this place is the one they take care of.”
Or rather, he is the one they will care for.
Have I not said many times here, when we were gathered together, “Whoever sees injustice being done, or any evil deed at all,
and does not tell me,
his blood will be on his own head”?
And to you yourselves, too, I said it with my own mouth when I came to you three times concerning the trials that had come upon us, saying to you while you were all listening,
“Whoever sees injustice being done, or any evil deed at all,
and does not send word to me,
his blood will be on his own head.”
And again, in the first letter,
I wrote to you, saying this:
“Whoever sees any evil deed among us here or among you yourselves,
and he does not tell me,
his blood will come upon him.
And so, why do you speak against one another secretly, in whispers, or openly,
grumbling against one another for no reason?
If there are some among you who see anything evil among us, why have you not told me?
Why are you bringing blood and everlasting judgment upon yourselves?
And if these evil things really exist among us—what you say secretly or openly, namely, “Those who have someone here
are the ones who will be cared for, or are the ones who are being cared for,
but the strangers and orphans are not looked after here, because they have no one”—
and so, if this great abomination exists among us, then why have you not told me, so that I might know?
Why are you bringing blood and everlasting judgment upon yourselves before God Almighty?
But if the things you say are lies,
secretly saying, “Those who have someone among us are the ones who will be cared for, or are the ones who are being cared for,”
then why are you sinning before the Lord, saying what is not true,
heaping up everlasting judgment for yourselves before God, who will judge everything?

If it is indeed I, or if it is the elder, who is committing this great abomination in the Lord’s congregations, while you secretly slander us, saying, “They look after no one except those who have someone,” or, “They do not look after anyone fairly at all,” then you are even more contemptuous than we are.
For sometimes you call us blessed, but at other times you insult us terribly in secret, off by yourselves.

And those whom we have brought down in humiliation among you have not told us how we have wronged them, or how we have treated them with contempt, so that we too might become slaves because of our sin. For we are miserable, poor people before the Lord, and this is not in our hearts at all, not at all.
If we forcibly lord it over a little boy or a little girl among us, let alone an adult man or an adult woman,
as though we were using them with an authority that God has not commanded—
rather, this alone presses us in our hearts: to serve one another according to the apostle’s command, “Through the love of the [?], serve one another.”
And this is why we do not want to humiliate anyone or cause anyone grief, either among us or among you yourselves,

except those who provoke God to anger through their disobedience and their refusal to be instructed, opposing the Lord’s law and his commandments in order to fulfill their evil desires through wicked deeds.
People like these will not find comfort while others are grieving with sighs because of them.
Nor will they see the joy of God while others are suffering inwardly in great affliction because of them.
And just as a righteous person who keeps the Lord’s law cannot receive comfort from sinful people who transgress the Lord’s law,
neither can those who transgress receive comfort from a righteous person who keeps the laws.
So it is with all of us: God and his Christ Jesus, his angels, and all his holy ones can never take comfort in us if we transgress the words of the Scriptures and all his commandments.
Nor can we ourselves ever receive comfort from God if we continually choose to pursue our sins,
while God and his Christ Jesus, his angels, and all who belong to him are grieved over us.
But if some among us rejoice falsely while remaining in their wickedness, while the Lord Jesus and his angels are grieved over them as they remain in their transgressions,
then these are truly hardened sinners who conceal their violence and their wickedness.

Therefore, let no one deceive some among us into rejoicing falsely in their wickedness when they hear words written in places that are not counted among the canonical Scriptures of the catholic church.
Rather, such writings exist to be read occasionally in this way: people should examine what is beneficial in them and put it into practice.
But they should leave aside the other things that are not beneficial, as they are.
Therefore, let no one deceive some among us into rejoicing falsely in their sins when they hear words written in certain places that say:
“Do not let sorrow find a place within you, so that you grieve at all.”
Therefore, we are not obliged to read them; we may read them only by our own choice,
and listen to them occasionally.
Instead, we are under a much, much greater obligation to read all the laws, the prophets, the apostles, and the writings of all the holy ones.
And we are required to meditate on them day and night, at all times, at every hour, and day after day,
because the entire fullness of divinity is complete within them.
Therefore, we ought to read and meditate at every hour and at all times on the words of the canonical Scriptures of the catholic church,
so that we may understand how the eyes of the prophets and apostles grew dim with tears, and so that we may become aware and repent of our sins.
As for the additional books, those that are not counted among the Scriptures, we are not to learn them by heart so as to meditate on them at every hour, but to read them occasionally if we wish.
But we must not read apocryphal books at all, as those who examined what is beneficial commanded us.
Therefore, it is not only that hidden books should not be read at all,
But again, what are books that others have written as instruction?
but there are also passages taken from hidden books and written into letters in books, as though this were proper.
These other writings, too, should not be read at all by those who have been instructed in the holy Scriptures.
Therefore, the canonical Scriptures are sufficient for us to read, so that we may understand what is beneficial.
And the books of our father Athanasius, the holy archbishop, are also sufficient for us to read in them at all times.

And the books of all the others who are like our father Athanasius, the man of God, are also sufficient for us to read in them. All their written words were first examined [?] in truth in the light of the Scriptures, so that we might be saved through their sound teaching.
Nevertheless, I too know that it is right to rejoice in the Lord at all times, as it is written.
But I also know that worldly sorrow brings about death, according to the Scriptures.
But do not let the hostile, evil demons deceive us through trickery,
and let us rejoice falsely [?] God is angry with us
and pours out his wrath upon us because we rejoiced while he was grieved.
Therefore, let us repent
and weep over our sins with sorrow, sighing, and great anguish of heart, knowing
For godly sorrow produces in us repentance without regret, leading to the salvation of our soul and our bodies.
—for where is it written in the Scriptures of the prophets and the apostles that they say,
“Do not let sorrow find a place within you, and do not grieve at all”?
How, then, could our holy fathers say, “Do not grieve,”
when they themselves mixed what they were going to drink with tears, according to the Scriptures, just as they also say,
“Our eyes poured down streams of water”?
Then again, “My eyes were troubled by weeping.”
And again, “My life has wasted away in anguish,
and my years in sighing.”
And again, “I walked like [?] those who mourn and those who are downcast.” And he said,
“This was how I humbled myself.” And in many places in the Scriptures they also tell us in this way
that this is how they grieved
and mourned very, very deeply, from [?] and the ancients.
Above all, the words written in the Gospels tell us
that our Lord Jesus himself, even more, began to grieve and to be distressed in heart, with very great anguish.
And this is how he said it,
“My soul is sorrowful to the point of death.”
not because he had killed a person, as we have destroyed the temple of God,
nor because
Whether male or female, all these blessings will come upon them from God. Everyone who prevents, at that time,
or even now, the reading of all the words written in that book, or those written in this letter and the others we have written,
or those we will write from this day onward—and those who prevent them from being read at that time
or even now—all these curses will come upon them.

But everyone, at any time, who makes an effort to have them read, or who is willing to listen to them, to observe them, and to put them into practice—all these blessings will come upon them. Therefore, I will not only instruct the brothers who are of one heart with us to take care of all the words we will write in that book, along with those written in all the letters,
but I will also instruct them to preserve my clothes, which I have torn many times, finally tearing them into two pieces when I was deeply distressed, even to the point of death.
Therefore, I will instruct the brothers who are of one heart with us, those who are alive at the time of my death, to lay out my torn clothes before those who come after us.
And everyone who hears, at that time or even now, all the words written in that book, or those written in the letters we have written, or those we will write,
and says, “What are these torn clothes, and all these written words, and all these curses?”
And they will answer and say, “Because the one who watches over the whole earth…”
And the one who passes through the whole inhabited world many times, secretly, at all times and day after day—that is, God—
also looked down upon us once in secret, and passed through our assemblies many times without revealing himself to any human being, male or female, except to his angels alone.
And they will say, “At that time the Lord was intensely angry with us, with great wrath.
And he turned his face away from us in great anger, to bring great curses upon us, along with terrible afflictions and severe trials, because we had sinned against him,
when Satan came upon us like a ravenous, roaring lion and struck what was in our care.”
And they will also say, “When we repented with great humility, with hunger and thirst and weeping with tears, without hypocrisy, God turned his face away from us,
and turned back his wrath, so that he would not punish us with great, terrible trials.
And he removed the whole curse from us and had mercy on us with great mercy.
And he blessed us with a great blessing, bringing his hand upon us gently and compassionately, refining us to purify us, as it is written,
‘I will bring my hand upon you and refine you to purify you.’
And again, he has removed wicked people from among us.
And sinners more than anyone else, as it is written, ‘But I will destroy those who are disobedient,
and I will remove all the lawless people from among you, along with all the arrogant, and I will appoint your judges as at first,
and your counselors as in the beginning.’” And they will say, “This is what God did for us, because we are his servants.
And the Lord disciplined us mercifully and rebuked us compassionately, because we are his children. He is our Father.”
And those who take care, or will take care, of all the words written in this book, now or at that time, will answer and say,
“Cursed is anyone who says, ‘These words, or the curses, or the blessings that this man pronounces, are [?].’”
And that they will not come upon anyone, as he himself says: “All these curses will come upon them at that time—or rather, now.”
And they will say, “Those who do not believe that the Lord has done all these things to us are dead.”
And they are strangers to the one who created them.
As it is written, “God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
What, then, does it mean that God is not the God of the dead, but of the living?
Surely not all those who have died are strangers to God, nor do all those who are alive belong to God.
If God is the God only of the living, and not of the dead, then how did the apostle say:
“None of us will live for himself, and none of us will die for himself.
For if we live, we will live for the Lord, and if we die, we will die for the Lord.
So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
For this reason Christ died and lived, so that he might be Lord over the dead and the living.”

Therefore, when he says, “God is not the God of the dead, but of the living,” he is saying that God is not the God of those who are dead in sexual immorality, defilement, theft, lying, false oaths, fighting, rivalry, envy, hatred, hostility, unbelief, and every evil deed.
And this is how the Lord Jesus said it in his words: “God is not the God of the dead, but of those who are alive in purity, virginity, goodness, righteousness, truth, and every good deed.”
And those who will uphold the words of this book, so as to take care of them at that time,
or rather now, will answer and say, “God, God, anyone who conceals the words of this book,
or takes offense at any one of all these words,
the Lord will bring upon them every curse written in all the Scriptures and written in this book, while they are on the earth.
And the Lord will bind the wrath of his anger upon them on the day of wrath and throw them down into the furnace of fire that burns with a great flame.”
According to the Scriptures, people who are not asleep will quickly hear those who call to them.
And those who are asleep, if you call to them repeatedly, shouting, will rise from sleep.
But dead people, buried beneath the earth or lying in the tombs, will not hear if people call to them loudly with many words.
Rather, they will truly become aware only with difficulty at the last trumpet, on the day when the trumpet is sounded and the dead rise imperishable.
In the same way, people who are alert in their diligence through awareness
and love of God will quickly hear the holy words of our Lord Jesus through those who teach them in the fear of the Lord. And those who are held back a little by forgetfulness and closed-heartedness—
these others too, if they are taught once and twice from the Scriptures by those who love them, will turn away.
